title: model-arch-performance-notes-llama-mistral-qwen-moe-runtime-profiling
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures runtime profiling notes and high-level benchmark observations for three model families (Llama variants, Mistral, and Qwen) with a focus on long-context behavior and MoE routing overheads. It is an iterative working doc summarizing experiments run on A100/H100 hardware, profiling traces, identified bottlenecks, and short-term mitigations to improve tail latency and tokens/sec for production serving.

Summary (short):
- Long-context workloads (>= 8k tokens) expose KV-cache memory bandwidth and attention kernel scaling as primary bottlenecks across all families.
- Llama variants benefit most from flash/fused-attention kernels; if fallback to cuBLAS matmuls occurs, latency doubles for long sequences.
- Mistral-like architectures (wide MLP intermediate dims) are matmul-heavy; matmul kernel tuning and persistent cuBLAS streams matter.
- Qwen shows higher memory pressure for chunked attention implementations; careful chunk sizing reduces redundant memcopies.
- MoE routing (top-1/top-2 gating + scatter/gather) adds non-trivial CPU+GPU synchronization overhead; dispatch imbalance and capacity factor are the main throughput killers.

Experiment setup (common):
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB and H100 80GB (mixed runs).
- Serving binary: runtime v1.12.3 (baseline), compare with local build v1.13.0-optim.
- Framework: Triton-based serving with custom fused kernels where available.
- Profilers: Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, torch.profiler (cuda=True), and runtime trace logs (per-request timing: enqueue, tokenize, forward, postprocess).
- Workloads: generation (sampling) and greedy decode. Seq lengths: 512, 2048, 8192. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 for latency and throughput tests.

Key profiling observations (detailed):
1) Attention kernel scaling (flash vs matmul fallback)
- For Llama-variant fp16 at seq=8192, when flash-attn was used, end-to-end token latency ~ 75-110 ms per token (H100). With fallback to cuBLAS matmul-based attention, latency ~ 180-230 ms per token.
- Hotspot: softmax+attn kernel and the memory reorder (transpose) step. Nsight shows attention kernels occupy ~55-65% of GPU time at long seqs.
- Mitigation: ensure compiled binary uses flash-attn and that attention contiguous layouts avoid extra transpose. Add a runtime check to fail fast if fallback kernels are selected for long-context models.

2) KV cache memory bandwidth and memcpy overhead
- For all models, KV cache writes/reads scale with seq length leading to GPU memory bandwidth saturation on A100 for seq >= 6k with batch>1.
- Observed big spikes in memcpy (device-to-device) when serving multiple concurrent streams.
- Short-term fix: pre-allocate large contiguous KV buffers per worker and use pointer bump allocation to avoid repeated cudaMemcpy operations. Evaluate NVSHMEM approach for multi-GPU shared KV in Dedicated deployments.

3) Matmul-heavy layers (MLP) and Mistral behavior
- Mistral-style layers have relatively larger MLP intermediate dims (larger GEMM shapes). Profiling shows matmuls (cublas/fused-GEMM) dominate ~45-55% of kernel time at seq=512 but stay significant at long seq as well.
- Optimization: ensure persistent cublasLt heuristics are warmed (warmup runs), and tune workspace and algo selection. For production, pin Mistral MLP to optimized cuBLASLt/onednn fused kernels when available.

4) Qwen and chunked attention patterns
- Qwen inference builds often implement chunked attention (to approximate long context). Profiling indicates overhead from chunk boundary copies and extra attention passes.
- Recommendation: experiment with increasing chunk size to reduce number of attention invocations and reduce per-chunk overhead; measure memory footprint tradeoffs.

5) MoE routing overheads (routing, dispatch, imbalance)
- Router cost (Top-2 gating) occurs on GPU and then requires scatter/gather to expert buffers: observed significant overhead even for relatively small expert counts (e.g., 16 experts).
- Two main issues: (a) imbalance — some experts receive far more tokens leading to stragglers; (b) small-expert-batch inefficiency — many small GEMMs underutilize the GPU.
- Measured: for an MoE 1B-expert model at seq=2048, routing+dispatch added ~30-45% extra GPU time compared to dense baseline for same total params (when capacity factor is small).
- Mitigations: hybrid batching (aggregate expert calls across requests), increase capacity factor to reduce re-dispatch, implement per-expert batching queues in the runtime, and fuse scatter/gather where possible. Also evaluate offloading gating compute to CPU only when GPU is saturated but keep data movement minimal.

6) Kernel launch / small-op overheads and CPU-GPU sync
- Observed high CPU-side overhead in the runtime when many small kernels are launched per token (layernorm, rmsnorm, residual add, gelu). For long-context, kernels multiply and CPU scheduling becomes non-negligible.
- Use stream aggregation and kernel fusion to reduce launches. Move control flow to GPU where possible (reduce roundtrips).

Benchmark highlights (representative numbers, H100 fp16, single worker):
- Llama-13B, greedy, seq=512, batch=1: ~2100 tokens/sec (p95 latency ~ 1.1s per generation of 512 tokens).
- Llama-13B, greedy, seq=8192, batch=1: ~260 tokens/sec; attention becomes dominant.
- Mistral-7B, greedy, seq=512, batch=4: ~5200 tokens/sec (good matmul scaling).
- Qwen-14B, chunked attention, seq=8192->chunk 2048: ~480 tokens/sec; chunk overhead about ~12% of total time.
- MoE-XXB (sparse expert model), seq=2048: effective throughput varies heavily with capacity factor and expert imbalance; observed 25-60% of dense-equivalent throughput depending on workload.

Notes on measurement quality and variance:
- Warmup: always run 10 warmup iterations before measuring — algos (cuBLASLt) and JIT kernels need it.
- Scheduling noise: experiments run during peak infra times show up to 10-15% variance; re-run in isolated maintenance window for final numbers.
- Use nsight system traces to correlate CPU scheduling spikes with spike in kernel launches.

Recommendations (short-term, 1–3 sprints):
- Add runtime guardrail: detect and log when attention falls back to matmul-based impl; surface to telemetry and alert on long-context fallbacks.
- Implement pre-allocated contiguous KV buffers per worker to reduce memcpy overhead.
- Add hybrid expert batching for MoE: collect in-flight tokens for 2–3 ms to build larger expert GEMMs. Add config knob to tune capacity factor per-customer.
- Tune cublasLt heuristics per model during model onboarding; store recommended algos in model catalog metadata.
- Increase chunk size default for Qwen-style long-context variants and measure memory/throughput tradeoff.
- Introduce per-route model profiling metadata to record whether optimized fused kernels were used (binary flag) and model-performance baselines at onboarding time.

Longer-term items (3+ sprints):
- Investigate fused-attention implementations with native support for MoE dispatch to avoid scatter/gather overhead.
- Explore NVSHMEM / CUDA IPC for Dedicated multi-GPU KV sharing to reduce duplication and D2D bandwidth.
- Work with kernel authors (flash-attn, Triton community) to upstream small-kernel fusions for common layer patterns (norm+linear+geLU).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantization impact: measure end-to-end latency for 4-bit quantized variants (Llama, Mistral) including dequant overheads.
- MoE capacity tuning: determine recommended capacity factor per typical customer mix (chat vs. summarization).
- Run controlled experiments on H100 NVLink vs. A100 for multi-GPU KV sharing efficiency.
- Create a small benchmark harness that reproduces the routing imbalance with synthetic inputs so we can iterate on hybrid-batching logic offline.

Appendix: quick checklist for onboarding a new long-context model into the catalog:
- Run attention-karma test: check for flash-attn fallback for seq=8192.
- Run matmul/MLP microbenchmarks to populate cublasLt algorithm cache.
- Run MoE microbenchmarks to measure expert imbalance and effective throughput at different capacity factors.
- Add model metadata tags: uses_flash_attention=true/false, recommends_chunk_size=N, quantization_compatible=true/false, recommended_capacity_factor=1.5 (if MoE).

Concluding remark:
This doc captures the current runtime intuition and actionable items from the last round of profiling. Many of the mitigation steps are low-risk and should be iterated rapidly (pre-alloc KV, hybrid MoE batching, kernel selection caching). Next: run isolated H100 maintenance window experiments to validate numbers and then update the model catalog with the recommended kernel/algorithm settings.

-- Alex
